name.en-US: Sts. John Fisher and Thomas More
name.pt-BR: Santos João Fisher e Tomás More

prayerExcerpt.en-US: Nothing can come but that that God will.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Nada pode acontecer senão aquilo que Deus quer.

meta.face: Fisher: a tall, lean man of about sixty-five, clean-shaven, with a long, gaunt, bony face — a high, broad forehead, prominent cheekbones above hollowed cheeks, a long, straight, prominent nose, large, wide-open pale grey eyes under high, thin brows, lines running down from the nose past the mouth, a long, firm chin and a thin, straight, closed mouth; grey hair hidden under the cap, and a steady, searching gaze. More: a man of about fifty-five, clean-shaven with the faintest shadow of stubble, with a straight-sided, rather square face — a broad forehead, a long, straight nose with a slightly rounded tip, grey-blue eyes under straight dark brows with a small vertical crease between them, firm, slightly sunken cheeks, a square chin and a straight, composed mouth with a hint of wry humour; straight dark auburn-brown hair falling to the ears under the black cap, the face in three-quarter view looking off to the side. Fisher is older, paler and much thinner; More is fuller in the face, darker-haired and fair-skinned with a light flush.
meta.basis: Both faces follow Hans Holbein the Younger, who drew and painted them from life: Fisher's chalk drawing of about 1527 (a long, gaunt, clean-shaven face with wide eyes) and More's 1527 portrait in the Frick Collection. Erasmus's 1519 letter to Hutten confirms More's fair complexion, auburn-black hair and blue-grey eyes.
meta.excerpt: Thomas More, letter to Margaret Roper from the Tower, 1534 (Rogers no. 206), in the modern-spelling text of the Center for Thomas More Studies, https://thomasmorestudies.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Letters-205-206-D-on-Conscience-10-9-2025.pdf; pt-BR our rendering. The feast has no proper formulary in the repo.
